overview.description: 63 Pedro is an advanced, high-scoring variation of the traditional American trick-taking game 'Pedro' (itself a derivative of All Fours and Pitch). Played with four players in fixed partnerships, it is famous for its massive point totalsâ€”a single round contains exactly 63 points. Points are awarded for capturing specific trump cards, with the King (30 points) and the 'Pedros' (the two 5s of the trump color) being the most sought-after prizes. It is a game of aggressive bidding and high-stakes trump management.

history.origins: Developed in the late 19th-century American South and West as part of the 'All Fours' family of games. The 63-point variant specifically evolved to make bidding more granular and exciting.
timeline: 1880s: Basic Pedro is popularized in gold-rush mining camps.
1910s: The '63' point system is formalized by inflating the King and Nine values.
1950s: Becomes a staple in rural community halls across the Midwest.
Present: Maintained as a competitive league game in specific regional pockets of the US and Canada.
history.evolution: The 'Left Pedro' (the 5 of the OTHER suit of the same color) is a unique mechanic shared with games like Euchre, making the trump suit mathematically larger than others.
history.cultural: Regarded as the 'Gambler's Bridge' because of the rapid point accumulation and the potential for a single hand to swing the entire game score.

setup.deck: 52 cards. Trumps include the 'Left Pedro' (same color 5).
setup.dealing: Deal 9 cards to each player. After bidding, the deck is 'filled' and players discard down to 6 cards.

rules.objective: Score 63 points in a round and be the first team to reach a target (e.g., 500 points).
rules.gameplay: Standard trick-taking. You must follow suit if possible, but you can ALWAYS play a trump even if you have the suit led.
keyRules: Follow the legal action constraints defined for 63 Pedro.
Round outcome is resolved by the scoring method: Scoring summary: Scoring follows the game-specific point or pot rules.
Winning condition: Score 63 points in a round and be the first team to reach a target (e.g., 500 points).

strategy.basic: If your team wins the bid, protect your Pedros! If you have a Pedro (5), try to play it when your partner is winning the trick with a high card (like the Ace or King). If the opponent wins a trick containing a Pedro, they get the 5 points, and you likely fail your bid.
strategy.intermediate: The 'King Trap': Since the King is worth 30 points (nearly half the round), do not play it early. Wait until you have drained the opponents of their lower trumps or until you are certain your partner can shield you with an Ace. Conversely, if you have the Ace, lead it instantly to smoke out the opponent's King.
strategy.advanced: Bidding Density: Because there are 63 points available, a bid of 40 is considered standard for a strong hand. If you bid 60+, you are effectively calling a 'Slam'. Only bid this high if you hold the King, Ace, and both Pedros. Defensively, if you see the opponents are close to their bid, sacrifice your Nine to prevent them from taking the King.
tips: The 'Left Pedro' (the other 5 of the same color) counts as a trump for all purposes. Treat it as a middle-tier trump card.
Don't forget the 'Two'. Even though it's worth only 1 point, the team that captures the actual card 'The Deuce' earns the point, regardless of who wins the trick.

play_card.description: Play one card to the current trick. If trump is led, must play trump if able; if plain suit is led, must follow suit or trump. Trick is won by highest trump, or by highest card of led suit if no trumps.
play_card.constraints: Must follow suit if possible, or may trump. If trump led, must play trump if able. Winner of trick leads to next.

draw.reason: This game has no draw-from-stock action.

discard.reason: This game has no discard pile.

pass.description: Decline to bid; remain in the auction. Bidding continues until three players have passed, then the highest bidder chooses trumps.
pass.constraints: Legal during the bidding phase when it is your turn. You may pass instead of bidding a number.

bid.description: Bid a number from 1 to 63 claiming your team will take at least that many points if you choose trumps. Each bid must be higher than the previous. Highest bidder names trumps and leads to the first trick.
bid.constraints: Legal during the bidding phase. Bid must be higher than current high bid. Minimum 1, maximum 63. Bidding goes around until three players pass.

trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Left pedro (other 5 of same color) ranks as trump between 5 and 4.

trickConfig.leadRestrictions: High bidder leads to first trick. If trump led, must play trump if able; if plain suit led, must follow suit or trump.

edgeCases.text: Left Pedro: the other 5 of the same color as trumps counts as a trump ranking between 5 and 4.
The trump two (low): the point is won by the team of the player who was dealt the card, not necessarily who wins the trick.

Dealer with more than 6 trumps must play multiple cards to the first trick so that after the trick everyone has 5 cards; only the top card of the stack counts for the trick; scoring trumps may not be buried.
If bidder's team takes fewer points than bid, they subtract the bid from their score; opponents always add the points they take.

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck comprising four suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades. Each suit contains thirteen ranks: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King, providing versatile options for various card games.
engine.suitDescription: Suits and ranks are as defined in the deck description above; no separate suit or rank set is used for this game.

engine.dealPattern: 3,3,3 to each player; after bidding each receives 4 more then discards to 6.

scoring.description: Each team keeps a cumulative score. Points are won by capturing scoring trumps in tricks (ace 1, king 25, jack 1, ten 1, nine 9, right pedro 5, left pedro 5, three 15, two 1). The two (low) is scored by the team that was dealt it. First team to 152 wins.
scoring.winCondition: First team to reach 152 or more points wins. If bidder's team makes their bid they add points taken; if not they subtract the bid. Opponents always add points they take.
